model: the household. We model households in
rather than individuals, because we want to abstract from the concepts of gender, marital status, and number of children. Furthermore, the household is the usual unit of account in tax data. Because
is primarily a fiscal policy model, it is advantageous to have the most granular unit of account be the household.
This last sentence will not be true once we start carefully modeling government benefit programs, which focus on individual members of the household.
